surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism involves the chemiadsorption of ZnCl2 molecules followed by a reaction with H2S to form ZnS, with the byproduct HCl being removed during purge steps.
evidence: The substrate was first exposed to a 660 ms ZnCl2 gas pulse, which resulted in the chemiadsorption of a monolayer of molecules on the surface. Conversion to ZnS was accomplished by application of a 660 ms H2S pulse to the substrate.
